rules.title: Reprisal protections for tenants (G.L. c. 186, § 18)
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not threaten or take reprisals against a tenant for reporting code violations, enforcing housing laws in court, or organizing or joining a tenants' union. Violators owe damages of 1 to 3 months' rent (or actual damages if greater) plus attorney's fees. A termination notice (other than for nonpayment), rent increase, or substantial change in tenancy terms within six months of such activity is presumed to be a reprisal.
rules.key_value: Damages: 1–3 months' rent or actual damages; 6-month rebuttable presumption of reprisal
rules.quoted_span: shall be liable for damages which shall not be less than one month's rent or more than three month's rent, or the actual damages sustained by the tenant, whichever is greater, and the costs of the suit, including a reasonable attorney's fee.
rules.penalty: Damages of not less than one month's rent nor more than three months' rent, or actual damages if greater, plus costs and reasonable attorney's fees
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenants of residential premises; waiver in a lease is void.

parsed.doc_summary: Massachusetts G.L. c. 186, § 18 bars landlord reprisals against tenants who report violations, enforce housing laws or organize tenants' unions. It sets damages of 1 to 3 months' rent and a 6-month rebuttable presumption of reprisal for termination notices and rent increases.
